questions.stem: A Born-Haber cycle is best described as

options.text: An application of Hess's law to ionic compounds for calculating lattice enthalpy
options.explanation: The cycle enforces enthalpy conservation around a closed loop.
It reuses Hess's law, adding nothing new.

options.text: A direct measurement of lattice energy

questions.stem: In the drawn cycle, the elements in their standard states are placed

options.explanation: The elements are the pivot of the cycle.

options.text: About a third of the way up, on a marked horizontal starting level

questions.stem: The arrows for creating gaseous atoms point upward because

options.text: The convention demands it regardless of sign
options.explanation: Arrow direction follows the enthalpy sign.

options.text: Ions form at the same time
options.explanation: Ionisation is a separate later step.

options.text: Breaking bonds to make gaseous atoms requires energy

options.explanation: Mass is irrelevant to the drawing.

questions.stem: In the sodium chloride cycle, the electron affinity arrow for chlorine points downward because

options.explanation: Physics, not aesthetics, sets the direction.

options.text: Gaining the electron releases energy, an exothermic change

questions.stem: The step that closes the sodium chloride cycle is

options.text: The lattice enthalpy, from gaseous ions down to solid NaCl
options.explanation: The loop closes at the ionic solid.

options.text: The enthalpy of formation of chlorine gas
options.explanation: Chlorine's element level is already drawn.

questions.stem: State the enthalpy values shown in the sodium chloride construction for atomisation, ionisation, electron affinity and formation.
questions.modelAnswer: Atomisation of Na +108, of half Cl2 +121, first ionisation of Na +500, electron affinity of Cl -364, and formation of NaCl -411 kJ mol^-1.

questions.stem: State where the elements sit on a Born-Haber diagram.
questions.modelAnswer: About a third of the way up, marked by a horizontal starting level.

questions.stem: Explain why the Born-Haber cycle can deliver a lattice enthalpy that no experiment measures directly.
questions.modelAnswer: Hess's law makes the enthalpy change route-independent: the direct gaseous-ion route equals the sum of the measurable atomisation, ionisation, electron-affinity and formation steps, so the closed loop solves for the one unmeasurable term.

questions.stem: Sketch the level order for the potassium chloride cycle: which steps climb and which descend?
questions.modelAnswer: Atomisation of K (+90) and of half Cl2 (+122) and ionisation of K (+418) climb; electron affinity of Cl (-349), formation (-437) and lattice formation descend, closing the loop.

questions.stem: The rearranged equation for lattice energy is

options.text: Delta latt H = delta f H x delta 1 H
Delta latt H = delta f H - delta 1 H
Delta latt H = delta 1 H - delta f H
options.explanation: The subtraction runs the wrong way.

options.text: Delta latt H = delta f H + delta 1 H
options.explanation: The long route subtracts from the shortcut.

questions.stem: For MgCl2, the chlorine electron affinity is counted twice because

options.explanation: Magnesium's two ionisations are separate terms.
It holds one magnesium per formula unit.

options.text: Two moles of chlorine atoms each gain one mole of electrons per mole of compound
options.explanation: The formula unit carries two chlorides.
Stoichiometry, not magnitude, drives the doubling.

questions.stem: The lattice energy of KCl from delta f H = -437, atomisation 90 and 122, ionisation +418 and electron affinity -349 is

options.explanation: That adds instead of subtracting the ion steps.
That adds every magnitude regardless of sign.

questions.stem: The lattice energy of MgO is much more exothermic than KCl's chiefly because

options.text: Doubly charged, smaller ions and two electron affinities (one strongly endothermic) enter the ledger
options.explanation: Charge, size and stoichiometry all deepen the value.

questions.stem: If a Born-Haber question supplies the lattice energy and asks for the formation enthalpy, you should

options.text: Identify the direct and indirect routes, then rearrange the same equation for the unknown
options.explanation: The logic is symmetric whichever stage is hidden.

options.text: Redraw the cycle from scratch with new rules
Divide the lattice energy by T

questions.stem: State delta 1 H for the KCl calculation.
State the lattice energy of MgO from the given data.
Explain why the asked-for stage is always the direct route in these calculations.
questions.modelAnswer: Hess's law equates the direct one-step change with the sum of the multi-step route; the question's unknown sits on the direct side, so subtracting the known long-route terms isolates it.

questions.stem: A cycle for calcium chloride uses delta f H = -796 kJ mol^-1, atomisation of Ca +178, of half Cl2 +121, first two ionisations +590 and +1146, and first electron affinity of Cl -349 (twice). Compute the lattice energy.
